<member name="M:Inno.Core.Execution.LifetimeScope.Cancel">
    <summary>
    Stops new registrations and invokes cancellation callbacks on the calling thread.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Callbacks must return promptly. Dependent resources remain owned while cancellation callbacks execute,
    including when another thread attempts disposal. A callback reporting pending work permanently blocks release.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.AggregateException">
    One or more cancellation callbacks fail.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Execution.LifetimeScope.Dispose">
    <summary>
    Releases a quiescent lifetime in reverse registration order, continuing after ordinary cleanup failures.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Pending retirement retains the current resource and all remaining dependencies for a later attempt.
    Concurrent or reentrant retirement reports pending work without invoking a resource twice.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    Tracked work remains active; drain it before retrying.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.AggregateException">
    Cancellation, work or resource retirement fails.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Execution.LifetimeScope.DisposeAsync">
    <summary>
    Cancels and asynchronously drains tracked work before reverse-order release.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Only use asynchronous disposal for thread-neutral resources. Control-thread owners must await their work
    and call synchronous disposal at their own safe point; this method does not marshal to an owner thread.
    </remarks>
    <returns>
    A task that completes only after work and resource retirement finish.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.AggregateException">
    Cancellation, work or resource retirement fails.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Execution.OwnerThreadExecution.Run``1(System.Func{System.Threading.Tasks.Task{``0}})">
    <summary>
    Pumps continuations until the owned operation completes, then restores the previous context.
    </summary>
    <typeparam name="TResult">
    The result produced by the operation.
    </typeparam>
    <param name="operation">
    Work that owns and retires every task it starts before returning. Async void work is not supported.
    </param>
    <returns>
    The completed operation result. Operation failures and cancellation propagate unchanged.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentNullException">
    The operation is null.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    The operation returned a null task.
    </exception>
    <remarks>
    This is a blocking host boundary. Callback-driven hosts use their platform synchronization
    context instead. Work that explicitly suppresses context capture is responsible for returning
    to the owner before accessing thread-affine resources.
    </remarks>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Execution.RetirementBarrier.TryComplete(System.Action)">
    <summary>
    Attempts retirement once at an owner-thread safe point.
    </summary>
    <param name="retire">
    The owner's retryable retirement operation; the barrier never retains this delegate.
    </param>
    <returns>
    True after retirement completes, or false while work remains within its deadline.
    </returns>
    <remarks>
    Wrapped pending failures retain their ownership semantics. A nested timeout is rethrown in its original
    exception tree. Ordinary sibling failures survive retries and are reported once retirement completes.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.AggregateException">
    Retirement completed after earlier ordinary failures, or the owner reported a wrapped terminal timeout.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:Inno.Core.Execution.RetirementTimeoutException">
    Work exceeded its deadline. The barrier remains terminally faulted and dependencies must be retained.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    The caller is not the thread that created this barrier.
    </exception>
</member>
